title: Minify rank width: one-chip sub-rank access controller
idea: Build an FPGA DIMM controller that addresses each x4 DDR5 chip independently through per-chip command buffering, so a random access activates one chip's row instead of 8-16 chips' rows.
why: Overfetch: random-access activation energy (graph, KV cache) could fall about 8x on existing DIMMs. The FPGA prototype costs about $250k.

title: Overbuild 120 tiers, fuse to 100: tier-level sparing
idea: TRIZ #16 Partial or excessive action: deliberately deposit ~20% more tiers than the product needs, add a per-block tier-remap register, and e-fuse out any tier that fails test (shorts, Vt outliers, weak capacitors). The process window can then be loosened (faster deposition, cheaper precursors) because whole-tier defects become yield-neutral.
why: Fact 2: turns compounding tier loss (0.99^100 ~ 37% yield) into >90% die yield, cutting 3D cost per bit ~2x at a fixed defect density.

title: Vertical charge-coupled columns store packets without access transistors
idea: Deposit a 3D-NAND-like gate stack around a single-crystal or recrystallized channel and clock the gate tiers in three phases to shift charge packets up the column to one sense node at the top, so 128 bits share one transistor and no capacitor.
why: Leakage physics: a buried potential well loses charge only by thermal generation, far below a transistor off-state tail (fact 3), and removing the per-cell capacitor sidesteps the charge wall (fact 1); a 128-deep shift at ~1 ns per step keeps access near DRAM class while density follows tier count.
note: 128 bits per sense node with no capacitor; doubts: transfer inefficiency in poly channels, shift energy and serial latency.

title: CCD imager registers: vertical charge-shift strings replace capacitors
idea: Adapted from CCD image sensors: a 3D gate stack wrapped around a vertical silicon or oxide-semiconductor channel stores bits as charge packets in potential wells under each gate tier; a read clocks packets down the string to a floating-diffusion sense node at the base, like a CCD vertical register.
why: Removes both 3D blockers, the capacitor and the lateral transistor (fact 2); ~4F2/N per bit with NAND-like one-litho-for-all-tiers cost; trade-off ~50-100 ns serial shift for 32-tier strings.
note: NAND-like one-litho tiers with no capacitor; doubt: serial-only access, transfer losses, destructive string read.

title: CCD fused into 3D NAND-style string: vertical shift-register DRAM
idea: Combine a charge-coupled device with a 3D NAND gate stack: 200 tier gate planes wrap one vertical oxide-semiconductor channel, and clocking the gates shifts charge packets held in surface wells toward a floating-diffusion sense node at the top. Each gate is both 'capacitor' and transfer switch, so there is no per-cell capacitor, contact or access transistor.
why: No 3D cell (fact 2) and charge wall (fact 1): ~0.1 fF wells suffice because the floating diffusion has gain; one hole etch stores 200 bits. Serial latency ~100-200 ns, hidden by striping each cache line across 512 strings.
note: No per-bit capacitor or transistor; doubts are transfer efficiency, dark current and clock speed in deposited channels.

title: CCD memory fixed: vertical bucket-brigade strings feeding one base sense amp
idea: 1970s CCD memory died because serial charge shifting made access slow. Keep its strength, no per-cell contact, but cap strings at 8 vertical tiers. Charge packets in gated wells along a vertical channel are clocked down into one sense amp at the base, the whole string is latched into SRAM in about 20 ns, and it is written back in reverse order. This removes per-tier staircase and bitline contacts.
why: Attacks the contact/staircase cost of 3D DRAM (fact 2). Because DRAM already overfetches 128x (fact 8), a serial burst costs little. Target is 8 bits per 4F2 pillar footprint.
note: 8 bits per pillar with no per-cell contact; doubt is charge-transfer efficiency and dark leakage in deposited vertical channels.

title: Eliminate cells: vertical charge-coupled shift-register strings
idea: Delete the per-bit capacitor, transistor and staircase: each vertical hole through 128 tiers is a CCD whose tier gates are tied to only 3 clock phases, so charge packets shift up to a single sense node at the top (128 ns worst-case serial access, pipelined bursts).
why: Water: one hole etch plus one channel deposition serves 128 bits with no capacitor module or tier contacts, so wet cleans and CMP per bit drop by >10x; also removes capacitor charge-wall limits.
note: ~10x density with no capacitor; doubt: charge-transfer efficiency over 128 stages in poly channels, dark current, serial latency.

title: Gain-cell NAND string with dual-gate bypassable read transistors
idea: [Box: storage-node gate | dual-gate IGZO 2T0C | series-string current sense | monolithic vertical string | Si | 3D-NAND hole-and-plate deposition] Build 2T0C gain cells along a vertical macaroni string like 3D NAND; each read transistor has a back word-plate that, driven high, forces it on regardless of its stored node, so unselected cells act as pass gates and only the selected cell's storage node modulates string current. Write transistors hang off a second vertical write-bitline in the same hole.
why: Attacks 'no manufacturable 3D cell' (fact 2) and the capacitor wall (fact 1): no capacitor at all, reuses 3D-NAND tier economics; 64-128 cells per hole could give ~5x bits per footprint vs 6F2 at F=12 nm.
note: NAND-like 2T0C string with bypassable read FETs; doubt: series IGZO string current too low for 10-100 ns reads.

title: Core-rope via-programmed 3D weight store, one sense per rope
idea: Revive Apollo's core rope, where a bit was set by whether a wire threaded a core: inference weights are encoded by whether a BEOL via links a rope wire to a shared sense node, written by maskless laser/e-beam via patterning in a mature U.S. fab and stacked 16 metal decks high, with one sense amp per 64 rope wires. Static weights leave DRAM, which keeps only activations and KV cache.
why: Doing DRAM's job with less: weights are often >50% of inference DRAM; rope bits cost ~5-10x less than DRAM bits and need no EUV, capacitor or refresh.

title: Wafer-scale DRAM bonded under a wafer-scale accelerator replaces HBM
idea: Substitute HBM stacks plus interposer with one full DRAM wafer hybrid-bonded face-to-face to a wafer-scale processor: each compute tile gets the DRAM directly beneath it through ~2 um-pitch bonds, and defective DRAM tiles are routed around by the processor's existing redundancy fabric.
why: Data-movement energy (fact 5): ~3-4 pJ/bit -> <0.3 pJ/bit and >10x bandwidth per mm², with no TSVs (fact 6) and no reticle-limited interposer.
note: ~10x lower pJ/bit and TB-class capacity under compute; doubts: accelerator heat on DRAM retention, matching redundancy.

title: Geiger-mode avalanche read of a hundred-electron storage node
idea: Shrink the storage node to ~20 aF holding ~100 electrons and wire it as the bias of a SPAD-like junction. At read the junction is armed above breakdown for ~2 ns: a stored '1' tips it into avalanche (gain ~1e5) and a '0' does not, then an active quench resets it.
why: Poisson statistics need only N >= 36 electrons for 6-sigma discrimination, and kT/C noise on 20 aF is ~2 electrons rms. Storing 31,000 electrons is an artifact of bitline charge sharing, so the capacitor shrinks ~50x, deleting the 60-75:1 pillar (fact 1) and 1-2 patterning layers (fact 4).
note: Shrinks storage node ~50x, but retention scales with C and avalanche dark counts/variability threaten read fidelity.

title: Bootstrapped T-switch gain cell zeroes leakage across its write path
idea: TRIZ #12 Equipotentiality + #25 Self-service: write the gain-cell storage node through two series transistors and drive their middle node from the cell's own source-follower output, the guard trick from electrometers and sample-and-hold circuits. The inner transistor then sees ~0 V drain-source, so subthreshold leakage collapses.
why: Fact 3: leakage down ~50-100x, stretching refresh from 64 ms to seconds with plain Si or oxide transistors.
note: Known guard/T-switch trick; demoable on MPW, area penalty limits value to eDRAM.
